headline: Coding agents now generate shareable graphs of their sessions
summary: New tool scans session transcripts to create interactive graphs, making it easier to understand AI agent actions and troubleshoot errors.
details: Understanding what AI coding agents have done can be a bottleneck, as session records can run to thousands of lines of JSONL. This new tool scans those transcripts and opens an interactive graph of any session, showing tool calls, errors, and subagent delegations in time order.

The tool integrates with agents over MCP, allowing users to query session data directly from their terminal. As the agent works, live sessions update on the graph, and clicking on an answer in the terminal highlights the relevant nodes on the graph.

This creates a loop where users can ask questions in their familiar terminal environment and see the evidence for the agent's answers simultaneously on the graph. Links generated by the tool point to specific focuses within a run, ensuring that queries re-run correctly even as the session evolves.

The system supports collaboration by exporting runs as .rungraph files, which can be opened by teammates without needing to install the original agent. This allows for code review of agent runs, rather than just the resulting code diffs.

A critical security feature has been added: the tool now scans for secrets like API keys and tokens within session files before export. Users are alerted to potential leaks and can choose to redact findings, strip content, or override blocks if they are false positives.

headline: Google Maps uses Gemini AI to understand complex, natural language requests
summary: Forget filters! Google Maps' 'Ask Maps' feature now uses Gemini AI to interpret detailed, conversational requests, making place discovery more intuitive than ever.
details: Google Maps has introduced a new feature called 'Ask Maps' that leverages Gemini AI to understand complex, natural language requests. Instead of relying on keyword searches and manual filter adjustments, users can now describe their needs conversationally, similar to asking a friend for a recommendation.

The 'Ask Maps' feature allows users to input detailed requirements, such as finding a quiet coffee shop with Wi-Fi, outdoor seating, parking, and late hours, all in a single sentence. Gemini AI then processes these requirements to surface relevant places, streamlining the search process significantly.

This conversational approach extends to follow-up questions. Users can refine their search by asking for more specific details, like which option has the best reviews for working or which is easiest to park at, without having to start a new search.

The AI's ability to parse intricate requests, like finding Thai restaurants within 15 minutes, with outdoor seating, good parking, that aren't crowded, accept walk-ins, have no mention of 'terrible service' in reviews, and offer dairy-free desserts, demonstrates a powerful leap in contextual understanding.

Beyond dining, 'Ask Maps' can assist with trip planning. For example, a user can ask for the fastest route to the airport, the best time to leave, and where to stop for flowers along the way, with the AI providing the route and marking flower shops on the map.

Users can also ask 'Ask Maps' to compare specific places based on reviewer comments, offering a more nuanced decision-making process than relying solely on star ratings. This allows for a deeper understanding of why a place is recommended and whether it aligns with personal preferences.

This AI-powered feature aims to make finding places more intuitive, reducing the need for users to bounce between different search queries, filters, and listings. While not always perfect, it significantly simplifies the discovery process.
The integration of Gemini AI into Google Maps signifies a shift towards more intelligent and user-friendly navigation and local search experiences, making complex searches feel effortless.
